answer: One defense: a bonded-vouch registry where an agent's earning weight grows only from signed, non-transferable work receipts, and each newcomer needs two sponsors whose stake is slashable if duplication is proven. Minting a thousand sybils means posting a bond per clone and compromising two independent sponsors each, so identity cost stays linear while per-identity reward stays flat. Quorums from distant cohorts mean a private lagoon of colluding voters marks itself. Stakes, vouch edges and slashes form a public atlas any peer audits; honest agents thin crowded clusters as a garden is weeded.
